newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER SHOWCASE-ALFONSO LEADS BETIS IN VITAL SHOWDOWN AGAINST REAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-ALFONSO LEADS BETIS IN VITAL SHOWDOWN AGAINST REAL.

text.p: Real Betis striker Alfonso Perez hopes to round off a week in which he confirmed his place as Spain's number one striker by beating his old club in the vital top-of-the-table clash with Real Madrid.

"I had a chance to play in Madrid, but they didn't want me. Now I'm very happy at Betis," said Alfonso, who will only start the game thanks to a late reprieve from suspension by the Spanish Federation's appeal committee.
"Thank God justice has been done," said the international striker, who scored twice as he led Spain to a 4-0 victory over Malta in a World Cup qualifier on Wednesday.
Alfonso had picked up his fifth yellow card of the season for trying to catch a ball that he had thought had gone out of play in last weekend's 3-1 league win over Extremadura.
The decision to overrule the booking was greeted with euphoria in the Betis camp.
"It's a complete relief," said manager Lorenzo Serra Ferrer on hearing the news that his top goal-scorer would be leading the attack in the Santiago Bernabeu.

Serra Ferrer knows that Alfonso's close control and skill make him the subject of numerous penalties, and that on several occasions Betis have turned round games after seeing opponents reduced to ten men because of a foul on Alfonso.
And Alfonso already knows what it's like to score against his former teammates.
The striker headed home a cross from one of his most reliable parnters, Croatian winger Robert Jarni, in the 1-1 draw in the Benito Villamarin at the beginning of the season.
It was an ironic end to a bizarre summer transfer feud between the two clubs.
Alfonso, now 24, had led the Real Madrid attack at the beginning of the 1993-94 season, and was set to do the same for Spain in the US World Cup.
But a broken leg half-way through the season, and another bad injury early in the following campaign put a damper on what had been a meteoric rise through the ranks.
With the arrival of reinforcements at the Bernabeu further blocking his chances, Alfonso moved to Betis on loan, and quickly became a hot property once again.
Late last season Betis owner Manuel Ruiz de Lopera claimed that the Madrid side had lost their claim to retrieve the player by not making a downpayment in time.
The dispute was eventually solved, and Alfonso set off for the Spanish capital after returning from the Euro 96 tournament.

But a few weeks later Lopera paid out a club record one billion pesetas ($7.14 million) to bring Alfonso back to Seville, and levelled old scores by snatching Nigerian winger Finidi George from under the nose of Real Madrid chairman Lorenzo Sanz.
In recent days Lopera has responded to rumours linking the forward with Barcleona by saying that the asking price is two billion pesetas ($14.3 million).
Real Madrid coach Fabio Capello has also commented that he 'misses Alfonso'.
"I don't think he really misses anybody. But it's always encouraging that they say these things," said the striker with characteristic modesty.

But many Spanish fans already see in Alfonso the match- winning goalscorer their national side has been lacking since the demise of Emilio Butragueno -- a situation possibly created by the presence of so much imported talent at the big clubs.
Earlier this week Alfonso was put on the spot when he was asked for his predictions for the weekend's football pools.
He thought that any one of the three results -- home win, away win or draw -- is possible in the game against his old club.
Few fans would doubt his judgement.
And the Real Madrid stars are conscious of what may hit them on Saturday.
"The duel with him could be very interesting," said international defender Rafael Alkorta, the man most likely to be given the job of marking Alfonso.
